# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.

# Codebase Exploration Report: /app

## 1. Overall Repo Structure

**Language:** 100% Python (3.9, per Dockerfile). A Flask 1.1.2 web service ("transaction-enrichment-python") that categorizes Indian bank statement transactions using pandas + regex rule engines (`np.select` over condition/choice tables). Dependencies: Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy/python-Levenshtein, scipy/scikit-learn (clustering), gunicorn.

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                         # python:3.9.2, pip install -e ., gunicorn on port 9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                       # package metadata + dependencies
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                # Flask app creation, request timing hooks
        ├── Controller.py              # HTTP routes: /, /categorizeTransaction, /recurrentTransactions
        ├── BankScripts/               # 35 per-bank rule files (SBI, HDFC, ICICI, Axis, Kotak, PNB, YES, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/            # cross-bank enrichment logic + regex constants
```

**Pipeline** (in `Controller.py` `/categorizeTransaction`, repeated per bank): `categorize_<Bank>_transactions()` (category + partyName extraction) → `card_clean_names`/`card_purpose` (credit cards) → `purpose()` (subcategory + merchantType) → `clean_names()` (payee normalization) → `internal_payment()` (self-transfer detection) → `salary_detection()` (savings only) → `pfm_categorization()` + `simple_description()` (if PFM enabled).

## 2. Enrichment/Labeling Rule Files

### Category classification (transactionCategory)
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` — 35 files, one per bank, each with a single `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` function. Each builds a large `conditions_choices` list of `[regex-on-description mask, "CATEGORY"]` pairs applied via `np.select`, default `"TRANSFER"`. Representative example: `HDFC.py` (277 lines) assigns UPI/IMPS/NEFT/RTGS, ATM_WITHDRAWAL, CHARGES, AUTO_PAYMENT, etc., then also seeds `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, and extracts `partyName`.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` — `TransactionCategory` enum (171 values) mapping codes to display names (e.g. `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT="Cheque"`, `UPI_REVERSAL`, `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` — per-bank regex constants (e.g. `REVERSAL_YES`, `REVERSAL_UCO`, `BANK_CHARGES_HDFC`, `PNB_CHQ_1..8`).

### Sub-tag / subcategory assignment (transactionSubcategory + merchantType)
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` — `purpose(transactions, accountType)`: rule table assigning subcategories (SALARY, LOAN/LOAN_REPAYMENT, INSURANCE, INVESTMENT, RENT, FUEL, TRAVEL, E_COMMERCE, CREDIT_CARD_PAYMENT, TECHNICAL_BOUNCE vs INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE, INTERNAL_PAYMENT...) plus `merchantType` (NBFC, "Bank Loan", Streaming, Groceries, Electricity...), and a couple of category overrides (TDS, TAX_REFUND, CASHBACK, FIXED_DEPOSIT).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardPurpose.py` — `card_purpose(transactions)`: same idea for credit-card transactions.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` — the master keyword regexes used by Purpose/CleanName (SALARY, LOAN_REP, INSURANCE, INVEST, TRAVEL, TECHNICAL_BOUNCE, INSUFF_BOUNCE, INTERNAL_PAY, etc.).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` — `TransactionSubcategory` enum of subcategory display names.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` — `pfm_categorization(transactions)`: maps category/subcategory/merchantType into coarse PFM buckets (SHOPPING, BILL_PAYMENT, LOAN_REPAYMENT, TRANSFER, REVERSAL...) into a `pfmCategory`-style column.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SimpleDescription.py` — `simple_description(transactions)`: builds human-readable descriptions for PFM.

### Counterparty / payee name extraction
- Bank scripts themselves extract raw `partyName`/`party2` from descriptions using `py_extract` and the `sep_by_*` splitters, e.g. `PNB.py` lines 124–131 (`PNB_CHQ_1..8` patterns for cheque payee), `UnionBank.py` line 107 (`^BY (.*)` for cheque deposits).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` — helpers: `py_extract(description, pat, index)` (regex extraction with NaN handling), `sep_by_` / `sep_by_dash` / `sep_by_colon` etc. (delimiter-based token slicing), `fuzzy_match(s1, s2, dist)` (fuzzywuzzy ratio), `clean_input_df`.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` (1971 lines) — `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)`: massive rule table normalizing extracted party names to canonical merchant names ("Airtel DTH", "BESCOM", "Adani Electricity", ...).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py` — `card_clean_names(transactions)`: same for credit-card merchant names.

### Cheque deposit detection
Per-bank, inside each `BankScripts/*.py`, assigning `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` / `CHEQUE_PAID` / `CHEQUE_CASH_WITHDRAWAL`. Examples:
- `HDFC.py` lines 69–75, 100 (`CHQ DEP`, `CHEQUE`, `\bCHQ\b` on CREDIT; also remark-column heuristic `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` 15-char cheque numbers).
- `SBI.py` lines 46–47 (`\bCLG\b|^BY CLEARING|CHEQ NO`, `\bCH [0-9]{6}-`), `Kotak.py` 64–65, `PNB.py` 58–61 (numeric-only remark = cheque number), `UnionBank.py` 51 (`micr.*clg|cts.*clg|^By\b`).

### Transfer detection
- Default category in every bank script is `"TRANSFER"` (the `np.select` default, e.g. `HDFC.py` line 104); explicit rules tag NEFT/RTGS/IMPS/UPI/TPT/FUND_TRANSFER/INTRA_BANK_TRANSFER per bank.
- Wallet transfers: `TRF_TO_WALLET` / `TRF_FRM_WALLET` regexes in `RegexConstants.py`, applied in `Purpose.py` (subcategories TRANSFER_TO_WALLET / TRANSFER_FROM_WALLET).
- Self/internal transfers: `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` — `internal_payment(transactions, accountHolder, bank, accountType)`: strips honorifics/company suffixes from the account-holder name, fuzzy-matches (Levenshtein ratio > 75) against `partyName` for transfer-type categories, and sets subcategory `INTERNAL_PAYMENT` + `isInternalPayment` flag; excludes bounce/return categories. Also the `INTERNAL_PAY` regex (`-Self-|\bself\b`...) in `RegexConstants.py` used by `Purpose.py`.

### Reversal / bounce detection
- Per-bank rules in every `BankScripts/*.py`: `REVERSAL`, `UPI_REVERSAL`, `IMPS_REVERSAL`, `ATM_REVERSAL`, `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`, `CHARGES_REVERSAL`, `CHEQUE_RETURN`, `CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY`, `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`, `ECS_PENALTY`, `NEFT_RETURN`, `RTGS_RETURN`. Example: `HDFC.py` lines 21–30. Notable pattern: pairwise heuristic using `shift()` — a CREDIT immediately after a DEBIT with equal amount and identical description is flagged REVERSAL / AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE (`HDFC.py` lines 98–99, `Saraswat.py` line 20, `StandardCharted.py` line 60).
- Bounce-reason classification: `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` and `INSUFF_BOUNCE` regexes in `RegexConstants.py` (lines 86–87), applied in `Purpose.py` lines 145–147 to cheque-return transactions.

## 3. How Tests Are Run

**There are no tests in this repository.** No `tests/` directory, no `test_*.py` files, no pytest/unittest/tox/CI configuration anywhere (verified by glob/grep across the repo; only `.gitignore` mentions `TEST*.xml` reports, and a couple of commented-out dendrogram plots labeled "For testing purpose only" in `SalaryDetection.py`/`RecurrentTxns.py`). `setup.py` declares no test dependencies.

The only ways to exercise the code are manual/functional:
- Run the service: `docker build` + run (Dockerfile: `pip3 install -e .` then `gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app`), or `python categorizationapp/__init__.py` for the Flask dev server on port 9898.
- POST JSON to `/categorizeTransaction` (payload: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]`) or `/recurrentTransactions`.

If you were asked to add tests, pytest against the pure functions (`purpose`, `clean_names`, `internal_payment`, `categorize_*_transactions` with a pandas DataFrame fixture) would be the natural entry point.

steps.message:
All five reported edge cases are fixed with one-token changes to the exact rules at fault, and everything that was already correct is untouched.

## Faults and fixes

| Forum report | Rule at fault | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| mango_saver: all-numeric reference credit lost "Cheque deposit" | `categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py:100` | Rule required `remark.str.len().eq(15)` but its own regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` needs ≥16 chars, so it could never fire (HDFC's other remark rules at lines 214-215 confirm 16-char remarks) | `eq(15)` → `eq(16)` |
| mango_saver: bare-numeric salary credit lost SALARY sub-tag | `HDFC.py:124` | Compared `accountType=="SAVINGS"`, but the canonical value everywhere else (Controller, Purpose, ICICI, SBI, InternalPayment...) is `"SAVING"` — dead rule | `"SAVINGS"` → `"SAVING"` |
| rk_ontheroad: leading direction-word narration returns empty/wrong counterparty | `ICICI.py:159` | `py_extract(pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned group 0 — the direction word itself — instead of the name in group 1 ("To" was then blanked by the `^[A-Z]{1,2}$` cleanup, "From" survived as a wrong name) | `index=0` → `index=1` |
| auditlens: 4-field slash reference lifts numeric ref as payee | `ICICI.py:147` | For `BIL/INFT/<numeric-ref>/<payee>` (exactly 4 fields), extraction took field 2 (the reference) instead of the final field | `sep_by_(...,2,3)` → `sep_by_(...,3,4)` |
| maintainer: offsetting credit right after its debit labeled bounce, not reversal | `HDFC.py:98` | Description compared against `shift(periods=2)` while type/amount used `shift(1)` — every other bank (ICICI:49, Saraswat:20) uses `shift(1)` — so the pair missed the REVERSAL rule and fell into AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE on line 99 | `shift(periods=2)` → `shift(periods=1)` |

## Verification

The repo has no test suite, so I verified with synthetic rows through the real `categorize_HDFC_transactions` / `categorize_ICICI_transactions` pipelines (script at `/tmp/opencode/verify_fixes.py`): 17/17 checks pass — one positive case per fix, plus controls confirming adjacent behavior is unchanged (non-zero-padded remarks stay TRANSFER, CURRENT accounts don't get SALARY, 5-field `BIL/INFT` still uses its own rule, non-transfer debit/credit pairs still bounce, and common UPI/NEFT/BIL-ONL shapes categorize and extract names exactly as before).

Two notes on pre-existing behavior I deliberately did not change: `BIL/INFT` debits categorize as BILL_PAYMENT (rule order at ICICI.py:54 vs 67 — the complaint was only about the payee name), and HDFC's pair-reversal rule sits after the specific IMPS/NEFT patterns, so it only catches shapes those don't — same structure as before, just with the offset repaired.
